actions.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: single rehabilitation exercise photograph.
Primary request: action 185, T-LOW-057 固定自行车的分段活动耐受训练: an adult woman gently pedaling a stable ordinary upright stationary exercise bike at an easy comfortable pace. One photograph, one woman, one clear moment of the pedal cycle. Do not put any title or number in the image.
Reference images: All three supplied photographs strictly define the SAME woman, SAME recognizable face, SAME dark ponytail, SAME white fitted short-sleeve crewneck T-shirt, SAME charcoal dark gray long pants, SAME normal adult body proportions, SAME natural skin, SAME soft realistic studio photography and SAME muted light gray-blue background color. Match the references closely. For footwear she wears simple white low-top sports shoes.
Scene: plain seamless light gray-blue studio backdrop and matching matte floor. No gym, room, decor or distracting objects.
Pose and anatomy: she faces right while sitting securely ON the actual saddle of a regular gray/black upright stationary bike. Her buttocks are clearly supported by the saddle at the correct hip position; she is not standing on the pedals or floating above the seat. Normal torso and normal length thighs/shins/arms, no stretched limbs. Her spine is neutral, torso almost upright with only a gentle forward inclination, head upright and calm expression like the references. Both hands rest lightly on a high comfortable handlebar; relaxed elbows, no racing crouch. Correct adjusted saddle height: the leg whose pedal is near the bottom of its circle remains slightly bent at the knee, not locked or hyperextended. The other leg is comfortably bent with its pedal near the top. The two crank arms are opposite ends of one realistic crankshaft (180 degrees apart), and each white shoe is placed securely flat on its own pedal. Both shoes, both pedal contacts, both knees and ankles are visibly distinguishable. One foot is down around five/six o'clock, the opposite foot is up around eleven/twelve o'clock. Natural comfortable movement range, no cramped extreme knee bend.
Bike: ordinary compact upright exercise bike with physically coherent saddle, seat post, high handlebar and handlebar post, central flywheel casing, exactly two pedal cranks, two individual pedals, and front/rear stable floor stabilizer bars. Gray/black matte metal and realistic rubber parts, no brand name. Bike chassis, saddle contact, crank mechanism, both feet on pedals and complete stabilizer bars must be fully in frame and readable. Avoid obscuring the far shoe and far pedal with the bike casing; choose a slight 15-degree three-quarter angle off a right-facing side view to separate both legs and both pedal contacts while retaining a mostly side-profile pose.
Composition: vertical 4:5, approximately 1122 by 1402 pixels, camera level with normal portrait lens and proportional human anatomy. Pull back enough that the complete woman from head through both white shoes and the complete bike including handlebars, saddle and all stable feet fit with clear margins. Do not shrink the torso or stretch legs to fit the bike. Soft reference-like studio lighting, photorealistic natural textures, gentle floor contact shadows.
Constraints: one woman, one bike, one pose. Exactly two arms, two legs and two feet. No arrows, text, numbers, logos, readable console display, watermark, panels, collage, secondary figures or therapist. No racing handlebars/crouch, no impossible crank alignment, no locked knee, no floating feet, no extra pedals, no cropped head/feet/bike.

correction_prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create one realistic studio rehabilitation photo of an ordinary upright stationary bike ridden gently by the SAME woman in the three supplied references. The references strictly define her recognizable face, dark ponytail, white fitted short-sleeve crewneck T-shirt, charcoal dark-gray full-length pants, natural skin texture, normal adult body proportions and the unchanged soft light gray-blue studio background color and lighting. Simple white low-top sports shoes. No image text.
She faces right in a mostly side view, camera only slightly angled 10–15 degrees to reveal both legs. She sits firmly ON the actual saddle, buttocks visibly supported, spine neutral and torso nearly upright. She has a calm comfortable expression and only a little forward inclination. Both hands lightly hold HIGH upright comfortable handlebars, elbows softly bent, not a racing crouch.
Critical mechanical geometry: show a simple physically correct pedal bicycle drivetrain: ONE round crankshaft axle at the lower center of the stationary bike and exactly TWO opposite crank arms connected to its opposite sides, 180 degrees apart. The NEAR/visible RIGHT foot is on the LOW pedal at the five-o'clock position (below and slightly to the RIGHT of the axle), and that knee is comfortably still slightly bent around 20–30 degrees. The FAR LEFT foot is on the HIGH pedal at eleven-o'clock (above and slightly to the LEFT of the SAME axle), with its knee bent comfortably. Both feet are on two real pedals, not on the chassis. The far foot and pedal must be shown clearly, choose open frame and narrow drivetrain casing so that neither shoe nor pedal contact is obscured. Do not put both pedals to the same side of the axle, do not put far foot on top of flywheel housing. The crank arms must be visibly physically connected and correctly aligned.
Bike: basic modern gray/black open-frame stationary bike, with small enclosed flywheel housing positioned away from the pedal contacts, saddle post and HIGH handlebar post, simple black saddle directly underneath her pelvis, two clearly visible realistic opposing crank arms/pedals and stable front/rear horizontal floor bases. It is a normal upright exercise bike used for easy rehabilitation, with no brand, no screen numbers. The entire machine and full rider fit naturally together, correct saddle height, coherent scale, no elongated arms/legs and no miniature torso.
Frame: portrait 4:5 approximately 1122 by 1402 pixels, complete head, hands, both knees, ankles, both entire white shoes, both pedal contact areas, saddle and complete bicycle including stabilizer feet fit inside with clear margins. Level camera, normal lens, no perspective stretching. Plain seamless light gray-blue photographic background and floor matched to original references, realistic soft shadows, no gym or room décor.
Only ONE woman, ONE bike, ONE pedal-cycle moment. No collage, arrow, number, text, logo, watermark, diagram, panels, therapist, other equipment, extra limbs, mismatched foot positions, floating person, floating shoe, standing on pedals, locked knee, extreme flexion, low racing handlebars or cropped bike.

Make a precise photorealistic pose/seat-height correction to reference image 4. Images 1, 2 and 3 strictly lock the SAME woman, face, ponytail, white short-sleeve T-shirt, charcoal dark-gray long pants, reference gray-blue studio background and lighting. Image 4 gives the stationary-bike composition and correct opposing-pedal arrangement to retain.
Correct ONLY the riding setup and pose: raise the saddle to a proper adult seat height and position the near pedal at the bottom of its circle, so the woman's near/right leg is visibly LONG and ALMOST EXTENDED, but the knee remains gently flexed around 20–25 degrees (included knee angle around 155–160 degrees). The current lower-pedal knee bends too much; this must be fixed. Do not lengthen or distort any body part. Move the saddle upward relative to the crankshaft enough to reach this proper setup. Reposition her whole natural body on that raised saddle. The near thigh and shin should form an almost straight relaxed line toward the near low pedal, with only a small knee bend.
Keep the far/left pedal at the top of the same crank circle, exactly 180 degrees opposite, and the far knee comfortably bent. Both white shoes must rest naturally on their own visible pedals, both sole-pedal contacts clearly visible, neither foot floating or standing on chassis. The same single crankshaft connects both exactly opposing crank arms physically. Preserve a clear stable gray/black ordinary upright exercise bike, actual saddle directly supporting buttocks, coherent saddle post and high comfortable handlebar post, full front/rear stabilizer feet on the floor. Her posture remains almost upright and neutral, only mild forward inclination, both hands resting lightly at the high handlebar, shoulders relaxed, calm face.
Pull the camera farther back as necessary so the complete head, hands, normal-length torso, both normal-length legs, both white shoes, all pedal contacts and the ENTIRE stationary bike fit comfortably within the portrait canvas with clean margins. Maintain NORMAL human head/torso/leg ratios. The seat height should look right for this adult woman's normally proportioned body. No racing crouch. A mostly right-facing side view with a slight angle to see both legs.
Same photorealistic style, exact muted light gray-blue seamless studio backdrop and matching floor, same soft lighting, 1122 by 1402 pixels, portrait 4:5. One woman, one bike, one moment. No text, arrows, numbers, panels, logo, readable screen, watermark, therapist or room décor. Exactly two arms/two legs/two white shoes, no extra pedals, no locked knee, no overlong limbs.
